mechanism_narrative: A 2% increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL over the prior 4 months signals anticipated inflation targeting by the Fed, prompting equity market anticipation of rate cuts and thus positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly change > +2% over the prior 4 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 4-month pre-trigger mean (p > 0.05), or CPIAUCSL does not exceed +2% over 4 months in 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly PAYEMS accompanied by a decline in UNRATE over the next month suggests improving labor market conditions and reduced wage growth pressures, leading to positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month AND UNRATE < previous month
regime_hint: Labor market improving but wage growth moderating
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in >50% of such labor signal events, or PAYEMS/UNRATE cross does not repeat in 5 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in GDPC1 (real GDP) followed by a positive HOUST reading indicates strong demand shock, predicting positive 5-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly > +3% AND HOUST > previous month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative when both GDPC1 > +3% and HOUST > previous month, in >30% of such events.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) exceeding 2% suggests supply-side weakness, which typically precedes equity market corrections and thus negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) when INDPRO declines >2% in 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in FEDFUNDS over the next 3 months indicates persistent monetary tightening, which is associated with negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS monthly > previous month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive in >40% of such FEDFUNDS tightening events, or FEDFUNDS does not rise for 3 months in a row.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in UNRATE below 3% combined with a decline in PAYEMS suggests weaker labor market conditions and increased recession risk, predicting negative 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when both UNRATE < 3% and PAYEMS falls in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly increase in RSAFS (retail sales) exceeding 5% signals consumer confidence and demand growth, leading to positive 5-day S&P 500 returns in an expanding economy.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not positive when RSAFS rises >5% in 2 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged monthly decline in GDPC1 (real GDP) with no offsetting strength in HOUST (housing starts) indicates structural supply constraints, predicting negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly < previous month for 2 consecutive months AND HOUST < previous month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not negative in >70% of such events, or GDPC1 recovers while HOUST remains weak.
